passage:
In the building corner of a kindergarten in Oslo, Ingrid and Oskar were stacking wooden blocks into a tower. “My turn!” Oskar said, grabbing the last flat block. “No, mine!” said Ingrid, pulling. The tower wobbled. Mila watched with wide eyes as it crashed. Both children shouted.

The teacher knelt beside them. “Oh no. What can we do so everyone can put one block?” Ingrid sniffled. “I go, then Oskar.” They built again, slowly, taking turns, and Mila got to put the roof on top.

qa.q: Who grabbed the last flat block?
qa.a: Oskar grabbed the last flat block.

qa.q: Why did Ingrid and Oskar both shout when the tower crashed?
qa.a: Both were frustrated and upset because each had wanted the turn and the pulling made the tower fall.

qa.q: What question did the teacher ask that helped?
qa.a: The teacher asked what they could do so everyone can put one block.

qa.q: How might Mila have felt watching the tower crash with wide eyes?
qa.a: Mila probably felt startled and a bit worried, perhaps wanting a turn, and was happy to place the roof at last.

grounding: Young children build a block tower together and argue over who places what, and an adult helps them take turns.

passage:
At the preschool's block corner, Tejas hugged the red truck. Ishita reached out. “I want it!” “Mine!” Tejas turned his back. Ishita's lip trembled. Rohan, sitting nearby, kept stacking blocks and said nothing.

Their teacher came with a small sand timer. “Tejas has the truck until the sand runs out. Then Ishita. Meanwhile, Ishita, can you load the blocks?” Ishita loaded. When the sand ran out, Tejas held out the truck. “Together?” he said, and they drove blocks across the mat.

qa.a: The teacher brought a small sand timer.

qa.q: Why did Tejas turn his back?
qa.a: Tejas was afraid of losing the truck and wanted to keep it, so turning away was a way to protect it.

qa.q: What did the teacher do that helped both children?
qa.a: The teacher set a sand timer for Tejas's turn and gave Ishita a job loading blocks meanwhile.

qa.q: What might Ishita have been feeling with the trembling lip?
qa.a: Ishita was probably upset and left out, wanting the truck and fearing there would be no turn.

grounding: Young children argue over a toy truck used to carry blocks, and a teacher's help makes turn-taking and building together possible.
